page: Microsoft Azure G2 is a G-family virtual machine powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2698B v3 processor. Operating on the x86_64 architecture under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. It is equipped with 56.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 14.0 GB per core. Additionally, the instance includes 786 GB of local storage, while offering zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks indicate that the G2 instance is constrained in raw computational throughput. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests, including stress-ng and Geekbench, place the processor's performance in the bottom 10% to 25% tier. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks also fall into the lower 25% bracket, though the PassMark memory score achieves an average rating in the middle 50%. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as AES encryption and gzip/bzip3 operations, consistently register in the weak category. For lightweight workloads, the instance manages average performance in small-scale LLM inference using a 135M model, but struggles with larger models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the G2 server trades off modern CPU processing speeds for a dense allocation of memory and local storage on legacy hardware. This makes it less suitable for compute-heavy tasks or high-throughput web serving. Instead, the resource profile is best aligned with memory-intensive workloads that require a large working set but moderate CPU utilization, such as caching layers, database hosting with moderate transaction volumes, or legacy enterprise applications requiring significant RAM and local disk space.
